mainTopic: Worshipped mountains, hills and trees, and how רבי יוסי הגלילי differs from the תנא קמא (עבודה זרה 45a)
overview: The משנה teaches that mountains and hills worshipped by idolaters stay permitted, but things placed on them are forbidden. רבי יוסי הגלילי learns this from a פסוק: 'their gods on the mountains', not mountains that are their gods. The משנה then asks why an אשירה (a worshipped tree) is forbidden. It answers that anything people had a hand in is forbidden. רבי עקיבא reads the same פסוק differently: it simply tells us where idol worship is usually found. The גמרא then asks why רבי יוסי הגלילי is listed separately, since he seems to say the same thing as the תנא קמא. רמי בר חמא, quoting ריש לקיש, answers that they disagree about a mountain's coating: is it treated like the mountain itself? רב שׁשׁת rejects this and says everyone agrees the coating is not like the mountain. His own explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Worshipped mountains and hills are permitted, but what is on them is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that mountains and hills worshipped by idolaters are not forbidden, but objects placed on them are, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If idolaters worship mountains and hills, the mountains and hills themselves are permitted, but whatever is on them is forbidden, as the פסוק says: 'Do not covet the silver and gold that is on them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a basic rule. The ground itself is not forbidden, but the items placed on it are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an object of עבודה זרה is forbidden for any benefit. Here the משנה separates the mountain itself, which is permitted, from the things on it, such as silver or gold, which are forbidden. The proof is the word 'עליהם', 'on them': what is on the idol is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the source text the גמרא will discuss)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main idea of the whole סוגיא: things that are part of the natural ground do not become forbidden even when worshipped.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The gentiles who worship the mountains
and the hills
they (the mountains and hills) are permitted,
but what is upon them is forbidden,
as it is stated:
"You shall not covet the silver and gold that is upon them."

steps.triggerLanguage: הַגּוֹיִם הָעוֹבְדִים אֶת הֶהָרִים וְאֶת הַגְּבָעוֹת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Worshipped mountains and hills are permitted. Items on them are forbidden, learned from 'עליהם'.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns the rule from 'their gods on the mountains'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads a פסוק to show that the Torah forbids gods placed on mountains, not mountains treated as gods.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: The פסוק says 'their gods on the mountains', which means the gods that sit on the mountains, not the mountains that are their gods. It says 'their gods on the hills', which means the gods on the hills, not the hills that are their gods.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי gives a second source for the same rule, taken from the פסוק about destroying places of idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה is to destroy 'their gods on the mountains'. Because of the word 'on', the target is what sits on the mountain, not the mountain itself. So a worshipped mountain is not included in the מצוה to destroy it, and it is not forbidden.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
"Their gods upon the mountains"
but not the mountains that are their gods,
"Their gods upon the hills"
but not the hills that are their gods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a separate source from the פסוק for why the mountains themselves are permitted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצוה to destroy applies to gods placed on mountains and hills, not to the mountains and hills themselves.

steps.title: Then why is a worshipped tree forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks why an אשירה is forbidden, since the same פסוק also mentions trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what reason is an אשירה forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה raises a problem with רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק continues 'and under every leafy tree'. By רבי יוסי הגלילי's logic, a worshipped tree should be permitted just like a mountain. Yet everyone knows an אשירה is forbidden, so his reading seems to have a hole.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that is worshipped as an idol

phrases.english: And for what reason
is an asheira forbidden?
phrases.notes: The same פסוק says 'under every leafy tree', so you would expect a worshipped tree to be permitted like a mountain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading by pointing to the tree case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading that worshipped natural things are not forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק lists trees along with mountains, yet an אשירה is forbidden. That seems to contradict the reading.

steps.title: A tree touched by human hands is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: An אשירה is forbidden because people were involved in planting or tending it, and anything with human involvement is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because people were involved with it, and anything that people were involved with is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question. A tree is different from a mountain because people had a hand in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mountain is pure nature: no person made it. A tree is planted or tended by people, so it is not purely natural. The rule is that anything with human involvement can become forbidden when it is worshipped.

keyTerms.meaning: Human involvement (literally: the grasp of human hands)

steps.whatToRemember: Things that are purely natural, like mountains and hills, stay permitted even if worshipped. Things that people had a hand in, like a planted tree, become forbidden.

phrases.english: Because there is in it
the handling of human hands,
phrases.notes: He means people planted or tended the tree; it is not untouched nature.

phrases.english: and anything that has in it
the handling of human hands is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ תְּפִיסַת יְדֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the אשירה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between untouched nature and things people were involved with
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A tree should be permitted like a mountain, since the פסוק mentions both.
steps.terutzMaskana: Human involvement makes the tree different, so the אשירה is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the פסוק only describes where idol worship is found
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads the פסוק as a description of where idolaters usually worship, not as a source for any law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: I will explain and decide this for you. Wherever you find a high mountain, a tall hill, or a leafy tree, know that there is idol worship there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא offers a different way to read the פסוק of 'on the mountains... under every leafy tree'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי read the words 'on the mountains' as a legal limit. רבי עקיבא says the פסוק is just telling us where idol worship tends to be: on high places and under leafy trees. On his reading, the פסוק is not a source for the mountain law at all.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of the פסוק. For רבי יוסי הגלילי it teaches a law about what is forbidden. For רבי עקיבא it only describes where idol worship is found.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:
I will explain and decide before you,
every place that you find
a high mountain and an elevated hill
and a leafy tree,
know that there is idol worship there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אֲנִי אוֹבִין וְאָדוּן לְפָנֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same פסוק that רבי יוסי הגלילי used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק describes the usual places of idol worship; it does not set a legal limit.

steps.title: Isn't רבי יוסי הגלילי saying the same thing as the תנא קמא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: רבי יוסי הגלילי seems to repeat the view of the תנא קמא, so why is he listed as a separate opinion?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: But רבי יוסי הגלילי is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and immediately asks a question about the משנה. It points out that two opinions in the משנה seem identical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said the mountain itself is permitted and only what is on it is forbidden. רבי יוסי הגלילי used a פסוק to say the same thing: gods on the mountains are forbidden, not mountains as gods. If they agree completely, the משנה should not list him as a separate view, so there must be some practical difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about the law itself. Both views agree that the mountain is permitted. The גמרא only wants to know what practical difference there is between them.

phrases.english: Gemara:

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא!
phrases.english: But Rabbi Yosei HaGelili is the same as the first Tanna!
phrases.notes: The first Tanna (תנא קמא) is the unnamed opinion from step 1: the mountain itself is permitted, but what's on it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's first two opinions (steps 1 and 2) and asks why they are listed separately.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's decision to list רבי יוסי הגלילי as a separate opinion from the תנא קמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both views rule that the mountain is permitted and the objects on it are forbidden. If there is no difference between them, one of the two opinions is redundant.

steps.title: They disagree about the coating of a mountain
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא, quoting ריש לקיש, says the two views differ about a mountain's coating. The תנא קמא forbids it, and רבי יוסי הגלילי treats it like the mountain, so it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said in the name of ריש לקיש: The difference between them is whether a mountain's coating is like the mountain. The תנא קמא holds the coating is not like the mountain, so it is forbidden. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds the coating is like the mountain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing to a practical case where the two opinions disagree: the coating on a mountain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views agree that the mountain itself is permitted. According to the תנא קמא, the coating is a separate thing that is on the mountain, so it is forbidden like other objects on it. According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, the coating counts as part of the mountain, so it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The coating or covering of a mountain
There is a difference between them

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer explains why the משנה lists two opinions. It also creates a practical question: may someone benefit from the coating of a worshipped mountain?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said in the name of Reish Lakish:
Whether the coating of a mountain is like the mountain is the difference between them.
The first Tanna holds:
The coating of a mountain is not like the mountain, and so it is forbidden.
And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili holds:
The coating of a mountain is like the mountain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ צִפּוּי הַר כְּהַר אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by identifying a practical case where the two opinions differ.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a practical difference (נפקא מינה) between the two opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two opinions seemed identical, so it looked as if one of them was unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: They disagree about a mountain's coating. The תנא קמא forbids it, and רבי יוסי הגלילי treats it like the mountain itself.

steps.title: Everyone agrees the coating is not like the mountain
steps.stepSummary: רב שׁשׁת rejects the previous answer. In his view, both opinions agree that a mountain's coating is not like the mountain and is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שׁשׁת said: Everyone agrees that the coating of a mountain is not like the mountain.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שׁשׁת disagrees with the answer of רמי בר חמא and ריש לקיש. He says there is no argument about the coating at all. This sets up a search for a different difference between the two views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both opinions agree that the coating is forbidden, the coating cannot be what separates them. The question from step 6 is therefore open again. רב שׁשׁת's own explanation of the real difference comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא צִפּוּי הַר אֵינוֹ כְּהַר.
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that the coating of a mountain is not like the mountain.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא צִפּוּי הַר אֵינוֹ כְּהַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 7's explanation of the difference, which reopens the question from step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the coating of a mountain is the point of disagreement.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב שׁשׁת holds that both opinions agree the coating is forbidden, so it cannot be what separates them.
